rites.name: Halostureld
rites.text: Halostureld is the concept of the Singing in Silia, the undated sounding by which the first roots of the world condensed out of silence. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between shores, the concept was remembered as the pull that drew scattered land back into a single voice.

rites.name: Lyirla
rites.text: Lyirla is the concept of the Seeding in Silia, the quiet season when the makers set the Weave into the ground and the sleeping powers are hushed beneath it. It is remembered less as a force than as a held breath, a stillness in which every sleeping power waits for its name to be spoken.

rites.name: Mialiel
rites.text: Mialiel is the concept of the Seeding in Silia, the stillness when the makers plant the Weave and the quiet powers sleep beneath the soil of the world. She is not a being who acts but a condition that settles over the Realm, a hush in which everything that might later bloom is held in waiting. Her presence marks the moment before creation becomes visible.

rites.name: Morastar
rites.text: Morastar is the concept of the Sundering, the flame that split the old world into shards and gave each one its own sworn law. In the Holy Age its name was carved above temple doors as the reason the Pact was made.

rites.name: Caulloria
rites.text: Caulloria is a concept of the flame-temples of Silia, born in the Fall when worlds broke and the Pact was sworn. It stands as a rite of ember and oath, kept by the orders of the Holy Age.

rites.name: Halernon
rites.text: Halernon is a concept of the Fall in Silia, the idea that a broken world can still hold its shape when bound by oath. It was given form during the Sundering, when the Shards drifted apart and the Pact was sworn to keep their edges from tearing further.

rites.name: Halenon
rites.text: Halenon is the concept of the wall-keeping, the disciplined holding of a line against the dark beyond the walls of Silia. In the Walled Age its orders taught that to stand firm is itself a kind of power, and its first crossings were marked as sacred acts of courage.

rites.name: Xaisheth
rites.text: Xaisheth is the concept of the Walls that keep the tides of the outer dark at bay, a notion held by the orders that tend the ramparts of Silia through the Walled Age. Its devotees describe it as the patient will that lets stone remember why it was raised. Chroniclers of the first crossings speak of it as the quiet power that bore the weight of centuries of holding.

rites.name: Thoneld
rites.text: Thoneld is the concept of the first sovereign's oath that a wall should hold for a generation. Within Silia's Walled Age it is the reason the groves were fenced and the first crossings were paid for in stone. The idea itself governs how long a kingdom's boundaries stay where they were drawn.

rites.name: Khathak
rites.text: Khathak is the concept of the holding wall, the idea that a boundary kept by many hands can stand against what lies beyond. In the Walled Age it was carved into the stone of every order and church, and in the Age of Sundering its keepers were the last to let a landfall pass unbroken.

rites.name: Alaama
rites.text: Alaama is the concept of the Walled Age in Silia, the long centuries when holding walls, orders and churches kept the peoples apart and first crossings were made by sea and by rope. It came to define how the Age of Sundering was remembered, when landfall broke the old bonds between shores and their keepers.

rites.name: Draggurn
rites.text: Draggurn is a concept in the Silia Record of the Mythic Realm, belonging to the Era E7 and tied to the Three Futures, where the ending of the world splits into branches. It is said to be the principle that lets the Library shelve every outcome as a separate, readable volume.
